Verified lint, tests and a production build in a tree copy, then QA's probes on that build (headless Chrome, real GPU). Every Chrome profile and the one server started were removed or stopped by PID.

QA's qpass/qsweep probes give 0 inside and 0 occluded frames on the production build. Also fixed: hedge and wall head clipping (collision standoff), lamp at the workshop entrance (lamp placement), Experience panel stray separator. assumptions: Only decor.ts lamp placement was edited in decor.ts, as the contract allows (LAMP_DOOR_X for the hall door lamps, two plaza lamp z values). No graphics-owned file was touched (materials, textures, sky, warm, resources, WorldView, GameAvatar).
A fade for camera-facing props would need material opacity in WorldView or resources, which the graphics-engineer owns, so the lamp is avoided by placement and guarded by a route test.
The collision standoff also moves the camera blocker (same collider), so the camera stops sooner against hedges and walls; analytic test blocks use the visual size, which is conservative.

The harness copies in the scratchpad used a patched h.mjs that creates each Chrome profile with mkdtemp and deletes it on close, exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM and failed start; 0 m3fix profile directories remain.
decisionsProposed: Camera in a pocket: lift first, then swing round the avatar by the smallest yaw, never force minDistance through a collider; only a sealed pocket uses the 0.45 m body floor.

Level colliders may be wider than their visuals (Block.standoff): 0.6 m for the hedge, 0.15 m for walls and buildings, so animation reach (head, hands) stays out of geometry without changing the layout.
Camera-facing props (lamps) stay at least 1.8 m from the trailing camera on the main routes, enforced by a route test, until a prop fade exists in WorldView.
lessonsProposed: A pocket test must sweep yaw through 360 degrees at both pitch limits while the avatar is pressed to the wall, over many wall faces generated from the layout, not a few hand-picked spots.
To prove a camera test is red on the old logic, neutralise exactly the new mechanism in a temp edit; just forcing the old clamp is not enough when the new search already avoids the pocket.
Hand-placed harness starts drift from the layout: assert in the test that the avatar really ends pressed to the intended wall.
Harness profiles: use mkdtemp plus rmSync on every exit path; verify with ls that none remain.
